About CRDC

Residents organising for a safer settlement

The Community Resilience Disaster Committee (CRDC) was formed by residents of 8ste Laan to reduce disaster risk, improve the local environment, support community development, and expand digital access for the settlement. The committee works closely with Ward 31, Subcouncil 15 and the City of Cape Town's Disaster Management team to raise and resolve issues that affect residents' safety day to day.

CRDC's work spans practical, on-the-ground projects — from anti-dumping and fire-safety messaging to documenting drainage and flood hazards — alongside the longer-term work of formalising the committee as a registered non-profit organisation, so it can access funding and formally employ community members through programmes like the Expanded Public Works Programme (EPWP).

NPO registration in progress with the Department of Social Development

FILE 01 🎨 Fundraising open

Anti-Dumping & Fire Safety Mural

2B Bream Way, 8ste Laan
Before
Design

A 30-metre wall, generously made available by the property owner, is being turned into a public safety message — split evenly between "NO DUMPING" and "NO OPEN FIRES ALLOWED." Wall permission is secured and the mural proposal has been submitted to the Ward 31 councillor's office. We're now raising funds for paint and materials.

Wall size30m × 2.1m
StatusProposal submitted
NeedsPaint, brushes & materials

FILE 02 🌧️ Active hazard

8ste Laan Drainage & Road Safety

8ste Laan stormwater channel

Farzaana Israel was shown the significant difference the completed section of the drainage channel has made, particularly given the heavy rains experienced over the past month. However, only half of the informal settlement area currently has a completed drainage channel — the remaining half is still outstanding. The committee is still waiting on Councillor Theresa Thompson to confirm when Nejeni Construction will return to complete the remaining work.

Farzaana Israel asked whether the committee has anyone responsible for keeping the drainage channels clear and clean on a daily basis. The committee confirmed that it does not currently have anyone formally assigned to this task — though committee member Ricardo Alfonso Major has since cleaned the completed section himself.

Cleaned
CompletedHalf of the drainage channel
OutstandingRemaining half
MaintenanceVolunteer-led, not yet formally assigned
Follow-upAwaiting confirmation from Councillor Theresa Thompson
FILE 03 📋 In progress

NPO Registration

Department of Social Development, Western Cape

CRDC's Constitution and NPO application have been drafted under the Nonprofit Organisations Act (Act 71 of 1997). The committee is now gathering the last outstanding member details — surnames, ID numbers and addresses — before formally submitting two signed copies of the Constitution to the nearest provincial DSD office.

FrameworkAct 71 of 1997
Year-end28/29 Feb
Next stepFormal submission
Also on the horizon

Early-stage initiatives for 8ste Laan. These will be updated with photos and progress as planning advances.

🏛️

Proposed Multi-Purpose Community Hall

Proposed Community Resilience and Development Centre (CRDC) facility at the identified 8ste Laan site. The concept provides a 14.0 m × 12.0 m site/building footprint, with an 80 m² main hall (10.0 m × 8.0 m), office (3.0 m × 2.5 m), kitchen (3.0 m × 2.5 m), store (3.0 m × 2.0 m), toilets (3.0 m × 2.5 m), covered entrance/veranda and an access ramp. The intended uses include meetings, training, community events, indoor activities, emergency shelter, administration, community catering, equipment storage and disaster-response supplies.

Proposed site identified
🛝

Recreational & Play Park

A proposed community recreational and children's play park on the vacant land identified along Robert Sobukwe Road. The submitted aerial and street-level views identify the proposed site. The concept includes landscaping, seating and children's play equipment, subject to planning approval and funding.

Document Policy

  • Official government forms and information will be used where available.
  • CRDC guides will be clearly identified as CRDC information and not government forms.
  • Outdated or superseded documents should be removed or clearly marked.
  • Completed applications and residents' personal information will not be published.
